chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who had intercourse with his wife and did not shorten (his ritual state), and he said: 'He slaughters a camel, and I fear that his Hajj may be deficient if he was knowledgeable; and if he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him.'
And whenever his intercourse was after the shortening (of the ritual state), there is no penalty upon him; what indicates this is what we have previously mentioned from the narrations.

And if he performed Tawaf and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah and shortened (his Ihram), then he has become free from every restriction he had entered Ihram for, including among those the intercourse of women.
And that is also indicated by what he narrated.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills in Mecca)
key_terms.تُقْصِيرْ: Shortening the state of Ihram by performing Tawaf and Sa'i
key_terms.جَزُوراً: A camel (specifically for the sacrifice in Tamattu')
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in a single journey

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who has intercourse before completing Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between major and minor Ihram restrictions for a Mutamatti' pilgrim, emphasizing that sexual intercourse is prohibited only while in the state of Ihram prior to completing Tawaf al-Qudum and Sa'i. The ruling differentiates based on the pilgrim's knowledge: a knowledgeable person incurs the penalty of slaughtering a camel (or sheep if unable), while an ignorant one is exempt, reflecting the Shia principle of leniency for those unaware of specific legal nuances. This highlights the critical role of Tawaf and Sa'i as the definitive markers for exiting the core prohibitions of Ihram.
